us-house.budget-law-energy: a budget law that ends the tax credits for buying electric vehicles and for new wind and solar power plants that begin construction after mid-2026 or begin operating after 2027, cancels unspent public money for clean energy, and requires two offshore oil and gas lease sales each year through 2040. By the official estimate, the tax changes are worth about 0.17 percent of a year's economic output a year over ten years
us-house.vehicle-waiver-revocation: a resolution, which became law, withdrawing one regional government's power to require that every new car sold there be zero-emission by 2035, a rule that several other regional governments had also adopted and that the regional government estimated would cut carbon dioxide from cars there by about 395 million tons between 2026 and 2040, about 6 percent of one year's national emissions
us-house.methane-fee-repeal: a resolution, which became law, ending a fee charged on methane emissions from oil and gas facilities above set limits, a repeal the official estimate put at about 0.002 percent of a year's economic output a year in forgone revenue
us-house.review-limits-bill: a bill, passed by the lower chamber but not yet law, that limits national environmental reviews of projects to the effects they closely cause, sets deadlines for agency decisions, and shortens the time to challenge a review in court from six years to 150 days, with no official estimate of how many reviews it applies to

uk-commons.carbon-budget-order: a legal cap on the country's greenhouse gas emissions for 2038 to 2042, set to bring them 87 percent below 1990 levels by 2040, at a net investment cost the government's assessment put at about 1.2 percent of a year's economic output a year
uk-commons.planning-infrastructure-law: a law that shortens approval of large infrastructure, among it power plants and grid lines, and lets builders pay into a national nature fund in place of meeting habitat protection duties site by site, which the government expected to speed up about 150 decisions on major projects within the legislative term and valued at about 0.1 percent of a year's economic output over ten years
uk-commons.nuclear-plant-decision: a final government decision to build a new nuclear power plant of 3.2 gigawatts, with public funding of about 0.5 percent of a year's economic output, producing enough power for the equivalent of about 6 million homes

de-bundestag.climate-fund-amendment: a constitutional amendment that creates a debt-financed infrastructure fund of about 11 percent of a year's economic output, to be spent over twelve years, of which about 2.3 percent of a year's economic output goes to the fund for cutting emissions, and that adds net zero emissions by 2045 to the fund's purpose
de-bundestag.heating-law-rewrite: a law that ends the requirement for new heating systems to run on at least 65 percent renewable energy and allows new oil and gas heating if it burns a rising share of low-carbon fuel, from 10 percent in 2029 to 60 percent in 2040, which the government said saves households about 0.1 percent of a year's economic output a year and whose effect on emissions it said it could not yet estimate

fr-assemblee.energy-programming-bill: a bill setting the national energy plan, which would have begun construction of about 14 new nuclear reactors adding 27 gigawatts by 2050, about 43 percent more than current nuclear capacity, and, as amended, stopped all new wind and solar power projects, and which the lower chamber voted down
fr-assemblee.low-emission-zones-repeal: a law abolishing the zones in 25 urban areas where older, more polluting vehicles can be banned, with restrictions in force in the two largest, which the constitutional court later struck down
fr-assemblee.farm-pesticide-law: a law that reauthorizes a banned insecticide of a class that harms bees, a provision the constitutional court struck down, raises the herd sizes above which livestock farms face fuller environmental permitting, for example from 151 to 201 dairy cows, and presumes new farm water reservoirs to be of major public interest

ca-commons.consumer-carbon-price-end: the end of the carbon price on fuels bought by households and businesses, which by the government's estimate gives up emission cuts of about 12.6 million tons from 2025 to 2031, about 1.8 percent of one year's national emissions
ca-commons.major-projects-law: a law allowing the cabinet to designate projects of national interest, which are then deemed approved under national laws on environmental assessment, fisheries, and species at risk, subject to conditions it sets, with projects worth about 4 percent of a year's economic output referred to the office it created in its first five months
ca-commons.regional-energy-accord: an agreement with one regional government that drops the planned cap on oil and gas emissions, which was to cut a further 13.4 million tons by 2030 to 2032, about 2 percent of one year's national emissions, and suspends clean electricity rules in that region, while that region raises its carbon price on industry to an effective 130 per ton and supports a new oil export pipeline tied to carbon capture
